main_text.l: Clamor] Contentio vocis. Exclamatio acuta. Vociferatio, Cic. Vociferatus, Plin.
Clamitatio] Plaut. Intentio vocis, Quint. Jubilatio, Apul.

Clamosus] Acutus & excitatus sonus. Clamatorius, Cic. Clamosus altercator, Quint. Argutus olor. Arguta fistula, Virg. Querulus, Hor. Tumultuosus, Plaut. Orthium carmen, Gell. Subtilissima vox, Id. Ejulabilis plangor, Apul.
Clancularius] Umbraticus homo, Plaut. Umbratica turba, Sen. Umbratilis vita. Clandestinum colloquium. Furtivum iter. Lucifugus, Cic. Timidus lucis, Sen.
Clara voce] Voce contentâ, exsertâ, summâ, Cic. Vid. Sonore.

Clare] Liquidò, liquidius, dilucidè, perspicuè, plane explicare aliquid. Explanatiùs luculentè, Cic. Illustrissimè describere. Demonstrativè, Macrob. Expositè, Gell. Nudè, Sipont. Sole clarius. Laternâ magis perlucidus, Er.
Clarescere] Effulsit sol in nubes. Dilucere, Liv. Elucidare lumen, Cic. Exsplendere, Plin.
Claritas] Candentia Lunæ. Prominentia in picturis. Eminentia, Vitr. Claror, Plaut. Fulgor, Cic. Claritudo, Fest.

Clarus] Splendidus. Candidus candor. Purus aër, Cic. Claror merus. Luculentus dies, Plaut. Illustris nox. Prænitens Luna. Prælucidus candore lunæ circulus. Occulatissimus locus, Plin. Liquidum lumen. Liquidissima cœli tempestas, Lucr. Pura luna, Cels. Veri luminis purpura, Trebel. Insolatus dies, Colum. Oculata dies, Plaut. Lucida gemma, Ovid. Percandidus, Cels.
Classicum certamen] Navalis pugna. Navale bellum, Cic. Navale prælium, Plin. Naumachia, Mart.

Classicum canere] Bellicum canere, Cic. Signum dare buccinâ, Curt. Inflare classicum, Virg. Convocatur classicò exercitus ad concionem, concrepantibus lituis. Processui canere, Amm. Insonant tubæ, Lucan. Classicum sonat, Seneca.
Classis navium] Castra navalia, Cæs. Navales copiæ, Tacit. Disjecta classis toto æquore, Virg.
Claudere] Adducere ostium cellæ, Petron. Obserare ostium.

page.notes: The text of the entries is set in small type; the ornamental fold mark across the right-centre is show-through/damage and was not transcribed. Entries are given as lines since each is a dictionary headword entry. Word "Clarâ voce" is read as printed; "Clamosus" headword reads "Clamofus" in print, copied as Clamosus with [?] not required but uncertain.
